title: Fixed Point Against Floating Point: Range and Spacing
unit: Computer Arithmetic: Fixed and Floating Point
quickIdea: Fixed point spends its bits on a constant absolute step; floating point spends them on a constant relative step, which buys range at the cost of a spacing that changes with the exponent.
remember: Fixed point Qm.n: spacing 2^-n at every magnitude, range about -2^(m-1) to 2^(m-1) - 2^-n.
Single precision: spacing 2^(e-23), so the spacing doubles with every increment of the exponent while the relative spacing stays between 2^-24 and 2^-23.
Fixed-point error is absolute and uniform; floating-point error is relative and uniform. That is the whole trade.
Floating-point hardware needs alignment, normalisation and rounding; a fixed-point add is one integer add, which is why DSPs and audio pipelines use it.
Neither format has 'more precision'. At 1.0 single precision resolves 1.19e-7, which a Q1.15 word (3.05e-5) does not; at 10^30 the fixed-point word cannot represent the number at all.
Exactness in a floating-point format is a property of the significand, not of the magnitude: 10^9 is exact in single precision, 10^9 + 1 is not.

example.prompt: Compare the spacing of single precision and of Q16.16 at 1.0, at 1000 and at 10^6.
example.work: Single precision spacing is 2^(e-23). At 1.0 (e = 0) it is 2^-23 = 1.19e-7; at 1000 (e = 9) it is 2^-14 = 6.10e-5; at 10^6 (e = 19) it is 2^-4 = 0.0625. Q16.16 stores an integer over 2^16, so its spacing is 2^-16 = 1.53e-5 at every one of those magnitudes - but its range stops at 2^15 = 32768, so 10^6 is not representable at all.
example.answer: The floating-point spacing grows with the value and the fixed-point spacing does not; the fixed-point range is the price of that uniformity.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: An 8-bit Q4.4 word and a single-precision word both hold 0.1. Which is more accurate, and which can hold 10^6?
variations.answer: Single precision is far more accurate (about 1e-8 absolute against 1/32 = 0.03125), and only single precision can hold 10^6.
variations.why: Q4.4 stores 0.1 as 2/16 = 0.125 or 1/16 = 0.0625, an error of up to 0.03125, while its range stops at 7.9375. Single precision resolves 0.1 to within 1.19e-7 at that magnitude.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does a fixed-point multiply need a shift but a floating-point multiply not?
variations.answer: In fixed point the product's binary point ends up twice as far from the right, so it must be moved back; in floating point the point is carried by the exponent, and adding the exponents does that bookkeeping.
variations.why: The shift and the exponent addition are the same operation on different representations of where the point is.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A DSP sums 10^6 samples of magnitude about 1 in a Q1.15 accumulator. What breaks first?
variations.answer: The range: Q1.15 holds at most 0.99997, so the running sum overflows after one sample.
variations.why: The accumulator's integer part is a single sign bit. A sum needs a wider integer part - Q16.15 in a 32-bit word - while keeping the same 2^-15 resolution.

trap.what: Saying floating point has more precision than fixed point, or assuming the floating-point spacing is constant.
trap.why: Precision is relative in one format and absolute in the other, so at a fixed magnitude either can win; and the floating-point spacing changes with every power of two.
trap.counterexample: At 1.0 single precision resolves 1.19e-7 while Q1.15 resolves 3.05e-5, so floating point is finer there; at 10^30 the fixed-point word cannot represent the number at all, which is a range failure rather than a precision one.

check.question: Is 10^9 exactly representable in single precision? What about 10^9 + 1?
check.answer: 10^9 is exact; 10^9 + 1 is not, and rounds back to 10^9.
check.explanation: 10^9 = 1953125 x 2^9, and 1953125 is below 2^24 = 16777216, so the significand fits. 10^9 + 1 needs a 30-bit significand, which the format does not have.
